issues.problem_description: Column `student_status` has too many distinct values for a status-like field.
issues.business_impact: Users asking for a single operational state will miss records because the same concept is represented in multiple ways.

issues.problem_description: Column `val1` has no meaningful business label.
issues.business_impact: AI BI tools cannot reason reliably about ambiguous field names, so this column will be skipped, misunderstood, or hallucinated around.

issues.problem_description: Column `enrollment_date` looks like a date field but is stored as free-form text.
issues.business_impact: Date filters, time-series trends, and comparison logic can silently fail when the platform cannot trust a field as a real date.

issues.problem_description: Column `revenue` contains a meaningful share of negative values.
issues.business_impact: Negative measures may be valid refunds or they may be sign errors. Either way, they need an explicit business rule before stakeholders trust the metric.

fixes.plain_english_fix: Map all status variants into a single controlled vocabulary before exposing the field to business users.
fixes.sql_snippet: CASE WHEN LOWER(TRIM(student_status)) IN ('active', '1', 'yes', 'true', 'enrolled') THEN 'active' ELSE LOWER(TRIM(student_status)) END AS student_status_normalized

fixes.plain_english_fix: Rename the field to a business-meaningful label and update downstream models to use the canonical name.
fixes.sql_snippet: ALTER TABLE your_table RENAME COLUMN val1 TO business_meaningful_name;

fixes.plain_english_fix: Normalize the field into a real date or timestamp before semantic modeling so filters and trends behave predictably.
fixes.sql_snippet: SELECT TO_DATE(enrollment_date, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS enrollment_date_date FROM your_table;

fixes.plain_english_fix: Decide whether negative values are legitimate exceptions or data errors, then encode that rule before reporting.
